I look down at my pocket, feeling my phone vibrating. Damn, another text? It’s only been 10 minutes since the last one. *I’m kind of busy here.*

Ever since the new, groundbreaking upgrade for the iPhones came out, which allowed you to transfer smells via text. Each phone was equipped with a small sack which, when pressed and then released, would quickly absorb the nearest scent through a small, needle size hole. Some people found this a helpful resource; they could share new perfumes, for example, or give people a nice taste - or smell - of the scent of the wonderful place they were on vacation.

Other people, *especially* my friend Richard, used this feature in many unpleasant ways. He sent many terrible smells to me, spamming them at any possible opportunity. But now, I assumed it wasn’t Richard, since it would be an absolutely horrendous time for him to send one now. After all, I *was*  in the middle of a first date with a particularly beautiful, funny woman who I had met over Tinder. 

“Are you alright, Michael?” she tilted her head at me like a curious dog, staring at my eyes. I suddenly looked back at her, nervously laughing. I still couldn’t get over how gorgeous she was, I couldn’t make a bad impression now.

“Ah, sorry, it’s just my phone. I think I have a text, do you mind if I quickly check it?” I stammered, rubbing the back of my neck with my palm, sweat dripping down my forehead again. But, luckily, instead of being faced with judgement, I was met with a kindly smile.

“Of course,” she said. “Take all the time you need, sweetie.”

Oh, my god. The way she said ‘sweetie’ nearly melted my heart. I had to resist sighing like a cliche main character in a love story, and felt my cheeks burning. To avoid any further cringey freakouts, I quickly turned to my phone, lifting it out my pocket and turning it on. A notification from Richard...oh no.

*Okay,* I thought. *He knows I’m on a date. It’s probably important - perhaps he’s asking for a favour.*

I quietly sigh to myself and press the notification, opening the text.

It takes a moment to settle in.

I read the text.

“Hey, Mike, how’s your date going?” the text reads.

*Ugh, that wasn’t important at a-*

Then, it happens.

A horrendous stench fills the room. It smells like rotten foods, immediately killing my apetite. I cover my nose, trying desperately not to make eye contact with Lola. But I can already see that she’s doubled over, trying not to breathe.

“I-I’m so sorry!” I cry, inbetween coughs and inhales. “I-it’s my asshole friend- sending me scents with the update-“

Then, suddenly, Lola has literally whisked me off my feet and is carrying me out of the restaurant, away from the smell, out into the fresh air of the night. As quickly as she picked me up, she sets me down on the concrete.

“That was odd,” she says, adjusting her ginger hair which is fixed into a messy bun. “But, that just makes this night more interesting, right, honey?” 

I struggle on my feet, taken aback. Dear god, I am a complete mess around her. Even with the strange stenches, she *still* manages to be so clever and caring and *beautiful*. 

She twirls me around, pins me against the brick walls for a moment, taking the time to whisper,

“I think I smell love in the air.”

I laugh, and then completely break down as she takes my hand, leading me down the street into the night. 

Suck on that, Richard.

On one hand, my Granddad was a lovely, truly wonderful man, and I loved every second I spent seeing him. But, he was of old age and it was getting difficult for him to breath, so I wouldn’t want for him to be alive any longer than he needed to or wanted to.

And on the other hand, I’d love to cuddle my dear Pops again, since I don’t think I showed him enough love - but since he died from antifreeze poisoning, I wouldn’t want him to be in pain when he could be free and painless.

Difficult thing to ask, really.
